Manufacturing industry 
Manufacturing enterprises in January -December 2018 pr oduced goods for 
175.4 trillion soums , growth rates compared to the corresponding period last 
year amounted to 113.2 %.  
Compared to the corresponding period of the previous year, the share of 
high-tech industries in the structure of the manufacturing industry was 1.6  % 
(1.9 % in January -December 2017), medium -high-tech - 29.7 % (21.7  %), 
medium-low-tech - 29.8 % (27.0 %) and low-tech - 38.9 % (49.4 %). 
The structure of the manufacturing industry for manufacturability   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
continued 
6 
 
 
 
 
Medium-high-tech productions of the republic made a significant 
contribution to the growth of manufacturing products - 9.6 %, the growth rates of 
which compared to the same period in 2017 amounted to 138.8  %. 
In the manufacturing industry, the share of enterprises for the production, 
repair, assembly of machinery and equipment, the production of cars, trailers, 
semi-trailers and other finished products reached 19.5  % (growth rate - 151.5 % 
by January -December 2017); the share of enterprises for the production of 
textile, clothing and leather products - 13.7 % (110.0 %), for the production of 
food, beverages and tobacco products - 13.2 % (96.3  %), the metallurgical 
industry - 11.2 % (105.7  %); enterprises producing chemical products, rubber 
and plastic products - 8.3 % (102.1 %). 
The overhaul of the process equipment allowed us to increase the capacity 
utilization of chemical enterprises and to exceed the production of the previous 
year in potassium chloride (108.6  % compared to January -December 2017), 
ammonium sulfate (108.6  %), ammonium nitrate (111.1 %), fertilizers nitrogen 
and other mixtures thereof (114.2  %), formaldehyde (118.3  %), paints and 
varnishes based on acrylic or vinyl polymers (134.5  %), superphosphates (1.8 
t.), mineral fertilizers containing nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (2.1 t.). 
The implementation of a set of measures to localize the production of 
agricultural machinery supplied to agriculture also contributed to the growth of 
products of medium -high-tech industries of t he republic. Compared to January -
December 2017, large enterprises increased  production: plows - 64.5 t., tractors 
- 3.4 t., grain harvesters - 19.4 %.

Consumer goods production 
As a result of measures taken to expand the range and stimulate the 
production of finished products, consumer goods produ ction amounted to 84.3 
trillion soums and, compared with January - December 2017, increased by 
15.9%, the share in the total industry amounted to 36.8 %. 
 
Structure and growth rates of consumer goods production in January-
December 2018 
 
 
Compared to the same period of 2017, in the structure of consumer goods 
in January -December 2018, there was an increase in the share of non -food 
products from 58.2 % to 68.8 %. 
In the structure of foodstuffs , the production of wine-vodka products and 
beer was 7.7 % (6.6 % in January-December 2017). 
 
 
 
continued

Production of enterprises with foreign investments  
During the reporting period, enterprises with foreign investment pro duced 
products to 94.0 trillion soums , growth rates to the corresponding period of last 
year amounted to 135.8 %. 
If in the previous year the share of joint venture products in the total 
production volume was equal to 35.1 %, then in the reporting period it increased 
and reached 41.1 %.

joint ventures in January-December of this year amounted to 12.3  %, ensuring 
the acceleration of the pace of reform and liberalization of the economy, as well 
as an increase in the competitiveness of products on the world market.  
In the total volume of joint venture product s, the share of mining and 
quarrying enterprises was 21.8 %, manufacturing industry - 78.1 %.

Industrial production of the regions 
In the structure of industrial output of the republic, the lar gest share falls on 
the Tashkent (18.6% of the republican industrial volume), Tashkent (15.3%), 
Andijan (11.8%), Navoi (9.9%), Kashkadarya (6.2%) and Fergana (5.6%) 
regions. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
continued 
14 
 
 
 
 
Growth rates of industrial production by regions in January -December 
2018, % 
 
 
 
At the same time, it should be noted that the largest share of consumer 
goods was produced in the Andijan region (25.3  % of the total consumer 
goods), Tashkent  city (23.6 %), Samarkand ( 8.7 %) and Tashkent (8.7 %) 
regions. 
The consistent implementation of measures to increase the industrial 
potential of the regions contributed to a significant increase in production in 
Andijan (155.8  % by January -December 2017), Khorezm (117.3  %), 
Surkhandarya (115.7  %), Tashkent (115.6  %) and Namangan (111.9  %) 
regions.  
At the same time, there was a significant increase in the production of 
consumer goods in Andijan (164.8  % compared to the same period in 2017),  
Khorezm (127.3 %), Syrdarya (111.2 %) regions and Tashkent city (111.8%). 
 
 
continued

Analysis of the differentiation of industrial output per capita showed an 
excess of the average national indicator (6944.7 thousand soums) in the Navoi 
region (23343 .2 thousand soums), Tashkent city (17123.9 thousand soums ), 
Tashkent (12160.0 thousand so ums) and Andijan (8867.7 thousand soums) 
regions. 
In the reporting period, production of consumer goods per capita in the 
republic amounted to 2558.9 thousand soums, including in Tashkent city 8010.1 
thousand soums, Andijan region - 7016.2 thousand soums, Navoi region - 
2691.2 thousand soums, Tashkent region - 2540.2 thousand soums.

The contribution of small business in industrial production 
The dynamic development of the industrial activity of small businesses 
ensured the growth of industrial production by the corresponding period of last 
year by 10.2 %, while the share of small business in industry was 34.7  %. 
In terms of regions, the largest share of small busin ess was observed in 
the Tashkent city (72.9 % of the total industry in the region), Namangan 
(68.5%), Jizzakh (64.4  %), Syrdarya (52.1  %), Samarkand (51.1  %), 
Surkhandarya (47.1 %) and Bukhara (41.1 %) regions. 
 
   
 
continued

 At the same time, the smallest share of small business was noted in the Navoi 
region (16.1 %) in the Republic of Karakalpakstan (18.7  %), Andijan (19.8  %) 
and Kashkadarya (21.4 %) regions.

Implementation of the program of localization of the production of 
finished products, components and materials 
 
The industrial development of the republic was also promoted by the 
implementation of the Program for localizing the production of finished products, 
components and materials, under which 714 projects produced goods for 15.0 
trillion soums, exported locali zed products - for 457.8 million dollars, 1092 were 
created new jobs.  
Compared to the same period last year, in January -December 2018 the 
volume of localized products increased 1.5 times. 
 
 
 
continued

However, compared with January -December 2017, there is a decrease in 
exports and the number of newly created jobs.

Most of the investment in fixed assets in the reporting period was directed 
to new construction. The volume of investment in new construction reached 
40,446.5 billion soums, which accounted for 56.9% of the total investment. 
Investments in the expansion, reconstruction, modernization and 
technical re -equipment of existing facilities amounted to 18,094.5 billion 
soums or 25.5% of the total. The remaining 17.6%, or 12,527.2 billion soums 
were directed to other areas. 
The largest share of investment in new construction was observed in the 
Bukhara region, and amounted to 73.6% of the total investment in the region. 
This is due to the project for the development of fields of the Kandym group 
with the construction of a modern gas processing plant. 
Accordingly, this indicator was 73.4% in the Republic of Karakalpakstan, 
68.5% in the Namangan region, 66.6% in the Navoi region and 64.8% in the 
Kashkadarya region. 
The lowest level of this indicator was recorded in the city of Tashkent, 
which amounted to only 38.2%

investment, of which 6,820.6 billion soums, or 9.6% of the total investment, 
were spent on natural gas production.

Construction work in the Republic of Uzbekistan 
 
January-December 2019 
The volume of completed construction work in January -December of the 
current year amounted to 68 854,4 billion soums. The growth rate compared to 
the corresponding period last year reached 119,0%. 
 
The volume of construction work carried out by large construction 
organizations amounted to 16904,6 billion soums. Compared to the same period 
last year, it increased by 8,5%, and their share in the total volume decreased by 
2,2% and amounted to 24,6%. 
       
 
THE STATE COMMITTEE OF THE 
REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN ON STATISTICS 
 
January-December 
2019 Construction work 2 
 
The volume of construction work performed by small enterprises and 
microfirms has increased significantly compared to other organizations that carried 
them out in the current period, whose share was 54,6% of the total, which is 4,6% 
more when compared to the corresponding period last year. Along with this, the 
volume of construction work they completed amounted to 37593,4 billion soums 
and, compared to the same period of the previous year, the growth rate reached 
129,5%. 
       
The share of construction work in the informal sector decreased by 2,4 
percentage points. and, compared with the same period last year, amounted to 
20,9%, or 14356,3 billion soums, the growth rate reached 108,3% compared to the 
corresponding period last year.

Construction work in the republic, carried out by state organizations, 
amounted to 3 899,2 billion soums, the growth rate reached 126,4%. The volume 
of construction work carried out by non -governmental organizations amounted to 
64 955,2 billion soums, the growth rate reached 118,5%, their share is 5,7% and 
94,3%,respectively.

modernization in the total volume of construction work 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Most of the construction work was carried out in the current period 
for the construction of new buildings and structures, 75.6% of the 
total volume of construction work, or 52 043,2 billion soums, were 
aimed at creating new production capacities in the field of economy, 
housing and communal services and other social facilities . 
Large construction organizations completed 
construction work on new construction for 14 888,8 
billion soums, or 88,1% of their total volume. 
Small enterprises and microfirms completed 
construction work on new construction for 24 597,2 
billion soums or 65,4% of their total volume. 
In the informal sector, construction work on new 
construction was completed for 12 557,3 billion soums, 
or 87,5% of their total volume.

for living.

compared with the same period of the last year, increased by 6,8% and 
amounted to 49,7 %. 
 
The share of the informal sector, compared with the same period last 
year, decreased by 2,9% and amounted to 28,7%.

The development of the service sector plays a huge role in the 
modern economy. Services generate key economic growth factors such 
as scientific knowledge, intangible forms of accumulation, information 
technology, and business integration. 
This sector of the economy includes various activities that help 
improve productivity and production efficiency. The final result is not a 
finished product, but the provision of services th at can be provided not 
only to businesses, but also to individuals – end consumers.

The service sector  is a consolidated generalizing category that 
includes the reproduction of various types of services provided by 
enterprises, organizations, and ind ividuals. This area is often referred to 
as a post-industrial economic structure because of its developed modern 
infrastructure.  
At present, intellectual human labor is gaining special development 
and value. its division creates a huge number of specialti es and 
professions that require special scientific training, a large number of jobs, 
a high degree of integration of joint human efforts and the growth of 
social welfare. 
These trends are directly related to the service and management 
sector, which leads t o its accelerated growth relative to other areas of 
human activity. It is characterized by higher profits than the industrial and 
agricultural sectors of the economy. The list of services is constantly 
expanding. 
As of January 1, 2020, the total number of operating enterprises 
and organizations in the Republic reached 398.1 thousand units.

For information:  Fitch Ratings affirmed Uzbekistan's long -term 
issuer default ratings (IDRs) in foreign and national currencies at BB -. 
The outlook on the ratings is Stable. 
According to experts, “ratings of Uzbekistan reflect, on the one 
hand, a good sovereign balance, low government debt and a history of 
high growth compared to countries with comparable ratings and, on the 
other hand, significant dependence on the commodity sector, high 
inflation and structural weaknesses in terms of "low per capita GDP and 
weak levels of the institutional environment and the quality of 
management relative to issuers with comparable ratings." 
At the same time, it was noted that “the government of the country 
is aimed at carry ing out reforms aimed at improving stability and 
improving growth prospects, as well as eliminating deficiencies in terms 
of the institutional environment and the quality of management. The 
authorities also intend to overcome the discrepancies between the 
objectives of monetary, fiscal and credit policies in order to strengthen 
monetary policy, reduce risks to macroeconomic stability and prevent 
rapid and sustainable accumulation of debt”. 
Currently, Uzbekistan has a score for relevance assessment: 
-  ESG 4  on parameter “Civil Rights and Freedoms”, since the 
World Bank governance indicators are the highest in the Fitch sovereign 
rating model and are relevant for the rating and rating factor. 
- ESG 5 on parameter "Political stability and political rights." 
- ESG 5 on parameter “Rule of law, quality of institutions and 
regulation and control over corruption”.

The service sector occupies a dominant position among the main 
directions of development of the modern economy. 
It is a complex multi -faceted mechanism and is one of the most

activities: from trade and transport to education and insurance.

educational institutions, travel companies, auditing and consulting 
companies, banks, clinics, motels, rest houses - all this relates to the 
service sector. 
The degree of development of the service sector ensures the 
territorial and soci al mobility of the population, the development of new 
economic territories, the increase in production efficiency and the 
consumption of material goods.

foreign countries. In particular, decisions to increase the country's export 
potential will allow local companies to gain more experience in foreign markets, 
which, over time, will give them a competitive advantage in world trade.

of January -November 2019, the foreign trade turnover of the republic for the 
reporting period amounted to 38,269.9 million US dollars and increased by 
9,588.0 million US dollars, or 33.4 % more than the corresponding period last 
year. Of this number, exports reached  16,255.1 million US dollars (growth rate - 
43.3%), and imports - 22,014.8 million US dollars (growth rate - 27.0%).  
A passive balance of foreign trade in the amount of 5,759.7 million US dollars.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER OF  
THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN 
 
(January-September 2019*) 
 
Reforms in our country contribute to the rapid growth of trade relations with 
foreign countries. In particular, decisions to increase the country's export 
potential will allow local companies to gain more experience in foreign markets, 
which, over time, will give them a competitive advantage in world trade. 
As a result of ongoing reforms in this directio n, according to the results of 
January-September 2019, the foreign trade turnover of the republic for the 
reporting period amounted to 31 645.8 million  US dollars  and increased by   
8 577.1 million US dollars or by 37.2 % more than the corresponding period last 
year. Of this number, exports reached 13 677.0 million US dollars (growth rate - 
45.5%), while imports reached 17,968.8 million  US dollars (growth rate - 31.5%).  
Marked a passive balance of foreign tra de in the amount of 4 291.7 million US 
dollars. 
 
 
 
*preliminary data

Uzbekistan has trade relations with more than 181 countries of the world. 
The largest volume of foreign trade turnover among the countries of the world 
recorded with China (18.7%), the  Russian Federation (14.9%), Kazakhstan 
(8.3%), the Republic of Korea (6.6%), Turkey (5.8%) , Germany (2.4%) and 
Kyrgyzstan (2.0%).

In the III quarter of 2019, the volume of foreign trade turnover amounted to 
11 962.6 million US dollars and increased by 16.4% compared with the second 
quarter of this year. 
 
 
 
In the III quarter, the share of imports in foreign trade  decreased 
compared with the II quarter (from 58.1 to 56.2%) and the share of exports 
increased (from 41.9 to 43.8%). 
Positive changes are observed in the dynamics of the quarterly structure of 
foreign trade turnover. So, the share of exports in foreign trade increased by 8.9 
percentage points compared with the third quarter of last year.

with the CIS countries amounted to 10 703.0 million US dollars, and the share in

The strengthening of socio -economic relations with neighboring countries 
also has a positive effect on mutual trade. For example, 37.7% of trade with CIS 
countries accounted for neighboring countries, including export - 42.6% and 
import - 33.9%. 
 
  
 
 
The share of other countries in foreign trade turnover in the reporting

sustainable economic growth of exports to achieve certain results. So, during the 
reporting period, the number of entities involved in the export of goods and 
services increased by 1  074 units compared with the same period last year and 
their total number reached 5 135 units. 
The volume of exports of the Republic of Uzbekistan in January -
September 2019 amounted to 13 677.0 million US dollars (increase d by 45.5%  
compared to the same period last year). The share of exported goods was 
81.4%, of which energy an d petroleum products - 16.1%, textiles and textile 
products - 8.6%, food stuffs - 8.4%, non -ferrous metals and products thereof -  
5.2 %, chemical products and articles thereof - 4.9%.

of Korea, Kazakhstan, Turkey, Germany and the United States) have a share of 
68.0% of total imports, amounting to 12 225.6 million US dollars.

In January -September 2019, the volume of imports of building materials 
amounted to 1 004.4 million US dollars and increased by 17.0% compared to the

reached 5.6%.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER OF 
THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN 
 
 
(January-July 2019*) 
 
International trade is a fundamental part of the economic activity of our 
republic. Ongoing reforms in this area allow saturating local and foreign markets 
with goods and services. Uzbekistan today is a country with an independent 
voice in the international community and a member of authoritative international 
organizations. Political -diplomatic, trade, economic  and cultural ties are being 
established with the leading industrialized countries of the world. 
The achieved trade relations with other countries contribute to the growth 
of exports of products manufactured in the republic, which, in turn, gives it the 
opportunity to become one of the developed countries of the world. 
 
 
 
 
 
* preliminary data

January-July 
2019 Foreign trade turnover of the Republic of Uzbekistan  2 
 
 
 
As a result of the ongoing reforms in this direction, according to the results 
of January-July 2019, the foreign trade turnover of the republic for the reporting 
period amounted to $ 24,526.8 million and increased by $ 6,834.0 million, or by 
38.6 % more than the corresponding period last year. Of this number, exports 
reached $ 10,880.2 million (growth rate - 44.5%), while imports reached  
$ 13,646.6 million (growth rate - 34.3%). A passive balance of foreign trade in the 
amount of $ 2,766.4 million was noted. 
Uzbekistan carried out trade relations with more than 167 countries of the 
world. The largest volume of its foreign trade turnover among the countries of the 
world was recorded with China (18.5%), the Russian Federation (14.6%), 
Kazakhstan (8.1%), the Republic of Korea (6.5%), Turkey (5.7% ), Germany 
(2.2%) and Kyrgyzstan (2.1%).

An analysis of the dynamics of foreign trade turnover also showed growth, 
and in January -July 2019 it amounted to 24 526.8 million US dollars, which, 
compared to the same period last year, increased by 6 834.0 million US dollars. 
 
Positive changes are observed in the structural dynamics of foreign trade 
turnover. So, compared with the same period last year, the share of exports  
in foreign trade grew by 1.8 percentage points.

 Due to traditional trade relations with the CIS countries and 
comprehensive support of foreign trade, the share of mutual trade with the CIS 
member states in the foreign trade turnover of Uzbekistan in January -July 2019 
reached 33.2% ($ 8,147.4 million), the pace foreign trade turnover growth, 
compared to the previous year, amounted to 119.5%. 
 
 
 
 
Current trade relations with other foreign partners also continue to develop. 
So, the share of other countries in foreign trade turnover in the reporting period 
reached 66.8% (16,379.3 million USD), the growth rate of foreign trade turnover, 
compared to the same period last year, amounted to 150.6%. 
Among the 20  major partner countries for foreign economic activity, there 
is an active balance of foreign trade with five countries, in particular with such 
countries as Kyrgyzstan (347.2 million US dollars), Afghanistan (315.6 million US 
dollars), Tajikistan ( 88.7 million US dollars), France (27.3 million US dollars) and 
Iran (16.2 million US dollars). For the remaining 15 countries, a passive balance 
of foreign trade is maintained.

In January-June 2019, Uzbekistan led trade relations with more than 166 
countries of the world. In particular, the foreign trade turnover of the republic in 
January-June 2019 am ounted to $ 19,683.2 million and increased by $ 4,520.0 
million, or 29.8% more than the corresponding period last year. Of this number, 
exports reached $ 8,437.6 million (growth rate - 27.0%), and import - $ 11,245.6 
million (growth rate - 32.0%). The fore ign trade balance amounted to minus 
2,808.0 million. 
 
 
Today, international trade is a fundamental part of the economic activity of 
our state. Continuing reforms in this area allow us to expand our markets for 
goods and services. Uzbekistan has become a country with an independent 
voice in the international community and a member of reputable international 
organizations. Political, diplomatic, trade, economic, and cultural ties have been 
established with the leading industrialized countries of the world.

amounted to minus 2,918.1 million. 
 
 
In general, the development of international economic relations contributes 
to sustainable economic growth of exports and imports in the country's foreign 
trade and, ultimately, the prosperity of our republic and the strengthening of the 
welfare of the people.

that includes the reproduction of various types of services  
provided by enterprises, organizations, and individuals. 
This area is often referred to as a post-industrial economic

The fruit and vegetable sector in Uzbekistan is an important segment  
in ensuring the food security of the country and regions. Therefore, in this area,  
all possible measures are being taken to accelerate the development of the 
production of fruit and vegetable products, which are yielding results. Thus,  
the volume of exports of fruits and vegetables amounted to 1 485.0 thousand tons 
and, in value terms, exceeded 1 008.6 million US dollars (the rate of decline, 
compared to the same period in 2019, was respectively 16.5%). Based on this, 
768.3 thousand tons of vegetables were exported in the amount of 400.0 million 
US dollars, as well as 402.3 thousand tons of fruits and berries in the amount of 
353.9 million US dollars (the rate of decline in value terms, compared to the same 
period in 2019, respectively amounted to 15.1% and 13.0%). 
The main export markets for fruit and vegetable products are in Russia, 
Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan. 
Such branches of agriculture as horticulture, horticulture and viticulture 
developed at an accelerated pace. Thus, in January-December 2020, the share  
of fruits and vegetables in total exports amounted to 6.7%.

in ensuring the food security of the country and regions. Therefore, in this area, 
all possible measures are being taken to accelerate the development of the 
production of f ruits and vegetables, which are yielding results. Thus, the volume 
of exports of frui ts and vegetables amounted to 1  387.7 thousand tons and,

dollars, as well as 381.8 thousand tons of fruits and berries in the amount  
of 339.2 million US dollar s (the rate of decline in value , compared to the same

The strategy for the development of the economy of Uzbekistan aims to 
create a diversified and competitive economy, the maximum use of national 
resources with the involvement of innovative technologies and new methods of 
market management. An importa nt role in this process is played by the 
development of foreign economic activity as the end result of the policy 
implemented in the country, which directly affects the standard of living of the 
population. 
According to the results of January -October 2020,  the кepublic's foreign 
trade turnover reached 30 059.4 million US dollars, which, compared to the same 
period last year, decreased by 4 256.9 million US dollars.

        Today Uzbekistan carries out trade relations with more than 160 countries of the 
world. The largest volume of foreign trade turnover was recorded with China (17.1%),

Turkey (5.5%), Kyrgyzstan (2.4%) and Germany (2.1%).

The necessary resource base has been created in the republic to ensure 
stable and uninte rrupted operation of enterprises and branches of the real 
economy. As a result of an increase in the production of products that replaced 
imported goods and the diversification of industrial production, significant 
changes have been achieved in the structure of exports. 
In addition, the strengthening of relations with neighboring countries is 
noted, a lot of work is being done to develop relations in the socio -economic, 
commercial, industrial and cultural sphere with these countries.  
              In particular, in recent years there have been significant changes in the 
FTT with neighboring states, for example, with such as Kazakhstan and 
Kyrgyzstan. The presence of an active foreign trade balance with Kyrgyzstan, 
Tajikistan and Afghanistan can be viewed as  a positive result in the country's 
foreign trade.  
 
 
             Among the 20 large partner countries in foreign economic activity, there 
is also an active foreign trade balance with four countries, in particular with such 
countries as Afghanistan (607.7 million US dollars), Kyrgyzstan (508.4 million US 
dollars), Tajikistan (242.3 million US dollars) and Iran (40.9 million US dollars).  
A passive balance of foreign trade turnover remains with the remaining 16 
countries.

in 2019, decreased by 12.0%.  
If we compare the indicators of the infographics of foreign trade turnover by 
months, we can see that in 2019 there was a stable dynamics of the FTT with 
minor jumps in June and July. 
The same figures for 2020 illustrate a different picture. Thus, if the first two 
months were at the level of last year's indicators, then since March there have 
been fluctuations characterized by changes in the situation on the world market. 
The sharp rise in the FTT in July and August was driven by gold exports. 
The FTT in September was marked at the level of 2 953.0 million US 
dollars. Compared to the same month last year, the decrease in foreign trade 
turnover amounted to 203.6 million US dollars.

The fruit and vegetable sector in Uzbekistan is an important segment in 
ensuring the food security of the country and regions. Therefore, in this area, all 
possible measures are being taken to accelerate the development of the 
production of fruit and veget able products, which are yielding results. Thus,  
the volume of exports of frui ts and vegetables amounted to 1  088.7 thousand 
tons and, in value terms, exceeded 696.1 million US dollars (the rate of decline, 
compared to the same period in 2019, was respect ively 27.4%). Based on this, 
581.5 thousand tons of vegetables were exported in the amount of 255.4 million 
US dollars , as well as 282.5 thousand tons of fruits and berries in the amount  
of 276.3 million US dollars (the rate of decline in value , compared  to the same 
period in 2019, respectively amounted to 31.8% and 16.8%). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The main export markets for fruit and vegetable products  
are in Kazakhstan, Russia, Kyrgyzstan and Afghanistan.

The strategy for the development of the economy of Uzbekistan aims  
to create a diversified and competitive economy, the maximum use of national 
resources with the involvement of innovative technologies and new methods  
of market management. An important role in this process is played by the 
development of foreign economic  activity as the end result of the policy 
implemented in the country, which directly affects the standard of living of the 
population. 
According to the results of January-August 2020, the foreign trade turnover 
(FTT) of the republic reached 24 537.2 million US dollars, compared to the same 
period last year, decreased by 3 554.2 million US dollars.

The necessary resource base has been created in the republic to ensure 
stable and uninterrupted operation of enterprises and branches of the real 
economy. As a result of an increase in the production of products that replaced 
imported goods, and the diversification of industrial production, significant 
transformations have been achieved in the structure of exports. 
In particular, in recent years there have been significant changes in the 
FTT with neighbor ing states, for example, with such as Kazakhstan and 
Kyrgyzstan. Among the 20 large partner countries in foreign economic activity, 
there is also an active foreign trade balance with four countries, in particular with 
such countries as Afghanistan (461.8 million US dollars), Kyrgyzstan (394.5 
million US dollars), Tajikistan (193.1 million US dollars) and Iran (39.6 million US 
dollars). 
 
 
 
             A passive balance of foreign trade turnover remains with the other  
16 countries. 
        Nowadays, Uzbekistan carries out trade relations with more than 160 
countries of the world. The largest volume of foreign trade turnover was 
recorded with the PRC (16.4%), the Russian Federation (14.6%), Kazakhstan 
(7.2%), the Republic of Korea (5.9%), Turkey (5.0% ), Kyrgyzstan (2.3%) and 
Germany (2.0%).

One third of the FTT volume falls on the CIS countries and, in recent years, 
this indicator has changed slightly. 
Despite the measures taken to strengthen cooperation with the CIS 
countries and comprehensive support for foreign trade, the share of foreign trade 
turnover of the CIS countries, compared to the same period in 2019, decreased 
by 3.4%. Over the same period of 2018, a decrease was noted by 8.7% and their 
share in foreign trade turnover, at the end of January -August 2020, amounted  
to 29.9%. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The volume of foreign trade turn over of other states in January -August 
2020, compared to the same period in 2018 -2019 (61.4% and 66.7%, 
respectively), increased and amounted to 70.1% of the  total volume of foreign 
trade turnover.

create a diversified and competitive economy, the maximum use of national 
resources with the involvement of innovative technologies and new methods of 
market management. An important role in this process is played by the 
development of foreign economic activity as the end result of the policy 
implemented in the country, which directly affects the standard of living of the 
population. 
At the end of January -June 2020, the republic's foreign trade turnover 
reached 15 855.8 million US dollars, which, compared to the same period last 
year, decreased by 3 528.0 million US dollars.

In January-June 2020, the volume of foreign trade turnover amounted to 
15 855.8 million dollars. And, compared to the same period in 2019, decreased 
by 18.2%.  
If we compare the indicators of the infographic of foreign trade turnover by 
months, we can see that after a slight decline in February 2019, there is a stable 
monthly increase. 
The same figures for  2020 illustrate a different picture. So, if in January 
and February the foreign trade turnover was recorded at the level of 2.9 billion 
US dollars, then in March there was a sharp decline to 2.2 billion US dollars 
(compared with February, a decrease of 25.3% ). 
During the same period, the largest decrease was noted in May at the level 
of 2  161.6 million  US dollars . Compared to the same month last year, the 
decrease in foreign trade turnover amounted to 1 158.3 million US dollars.

stable and uninterrupted operation of enterprises and branches of the real 
economy. As a result of an increase in the production of products that replaced 
imported goods, and the diversification of industria l production, significant 
changes have been achieved in the structure of exports. 
In addition, the strengthening of relations with neighboring states is 
noted, a lot of work is being done to develop relations in the socio -economic, 
commercial, industrial and cultural spheres with these countries.  
In particular, in recent years there have been significant changes in the 
FTT with neighboring states, such as Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. The presence 
of an active foreign trade balance with Kyrgyzstan, Tajikista n and Afghanistan 
can be viewed as a positive result in the country's foreign trade.  
 
Among the 20 large partner countries in foreign economic activity, there is 
also an active foreign trade balance with five countries, in particular with such 
countries as Afghanistan (330.5 million US dollars), Kyrgyzstan (281.5 million US 
dollars), Tajikistan ( US $ 141.7 million), France (US $ 14.4 million) and the UAE 
(US $ 8.1 million). The remaining 15 countries maintain a passive balance of 
foreign trade turnover.

ensuring the food security of the country and regions. Therefore, in this area, all

169.8 million US dollars (the rate of decline in value terms, compared to the

     As the investment climate in the country improves and as a result of 
reforms implemented in this area, the growth of imports of machinery and 
transport equipment is natural. So, taking into account the large volumes of 
investments from China, Korea, Russia, Germany and Turkey, a high share of 
these countries in the volume of imports of these products remains. 
 
 
 
 
 
The volume of imports of services in January -June 2020 amounted to 
657.4 million US dollars, or 6.9% of its total volume, and decreased, compared to 
the same period in 2019, by 39.6%. Travel (tourism - 47.2%) and transport 
services (14.7%) make up the bulk of imports of services. In addition, other 
services accounted for 25.9% of total imports of services, including a high share 
in telecommunications, computer and information services (8.4%), fees for the 
use of intellectual property (7.6%), construction services (4.3%), etc. 
 
 
 
 
At the end of January -June 2020, the volume of imports of building 
materials in its total volume amounted to 5.1% and reached 489.4 million US 
dollars. In its structure, the main share is occupied by wood and wood products 
(47.4%), cement (7.7%), glass and glass products (5.8%), as well as asbestos 
(2.3%).

The coronavirus pandemic (COVID -19), which has now 
spread to almost all countries of the world, has led to a decrease 
in international integration and the closure of state borders, which 
directly affects foreign trade and the standard of living of the state. 
According to the results of January -March 2020, the foreign 
trade turnover  (FTT) of the republic reached 8 140.4 million US 
dollars, which, compared to the same period last year, decreased 
by 924.1 million US dollars.  
 
For reference: in compili ng statistics on foreign trade in goods of the 
Republic of Uzbekistan, the United Nations International Standard Trade 
Classification (hereinafter - SITC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes 
to group exported and imported goods. Assignment of SIT C codes to goods is 
carried out using transition keys between the HS and SITC.

     Significant changes were achieved in the structure of 
exports as a result of an increase in the production of products 
that replaced imported goods and the diversif ication of industrial 
production. 
Uzbekistan has trade relations with more than 150 countries of 
the world. The largest volume of its foreign trade turnover among 
them was recorded with the Russian Federation (16.9%), China 
(16.8%), Kazakhstan (8.3%), the Republic of Korea (6.7%), 
Turkey (5.8%) , Kyrgyzstan (2.3%) and Germany (2.1%).

Currently, the volume of services in the ICT, content and media sectors is 
formed in accordance with the definitions presented in the International Standard 
Industrial Classification of All Economic Activities (ISIC-4) from the volumes of 
certain types of services according to the Statistical Classifier of Products 
(Goods, Works, Services) by types of economic activities of the Republic of 
Uzbekistan (UPC), interconnected with OKED-2 at the four-digit level and 
“Statistical classification of products by activity in the European Economic 
Community” - CPA 2008.  
 
The growing demand for data related to the information economy (information

in the field of rent and rental (32.3%), financial services (18.2%),

of architecture, engineering surveys, technical testing and analysis 
(11.4%), as well as in the field of education (5.7%).

was recorded in the field of transport services (by 9.9%).

observed in services in the field of architecture, engineering surveys,

In the structure of provided market services by type of economic 
activity, trade services account for the largest share. In January 2021,

repair services, which share reached only 1.6%. 
For comparison: in January 2020, trade services in the total 
volume amounted to 26.4%. For the same period in 2020, the share of 
computer repair services was also minimal - 1.6%.  
 
In January 2021, high growth was achieved in rent and rental 
services (46.3%), financial services (19.0%), education services 
(17.9%), communications and information services (13.4 %). 
A significant decrease in the volume of market services provided 
was recorded in the transport services (by 9.9%) and healthcare  
(by 0.5%). 
For comparison: in January 2020, high growth rates were 
recorded in financial services - 136.9%. A slight increase was observed 
in services in the field of architecture, engineering surveys, technical 
testing and analysis - 0.2%.

The main export markets for fruit and vegetable products are in Kazakhstan, 
Russia, China and Kyrgyzstan.

developed at an accelerated pace. Thus, in January-February 2021, the share  
of fruits and vegetables in total exports amounted to 5.8%. 
17 
The fruit and vegetable sector in Uzbekistan is an important segment  
in ensuring the food security of the country and regions. Therefore, in this area, all 
possible measures are being taken to accelerate the development of  
the production of fruit and vegetable products, which are yielding results. Thus, 
the volume of exports of fruits and vegetables amounted to 131.3 thousand tons 
and, in value terms, exceeded 86.6 million US dollars (the growth rate, compared 
to the same period in 2020, respectively, amounted to 7.5%). Based on this, 95.0 
thousand tons of vegetables were exported in the amount of 52.4 million US 
dollars (the growth rate in value terms, compared to the same period in 2020, 
respectively, amounted to 23.6%), as well as 19.6 thousand tons of fruits and 
berries in the amount of 16.7 million US dollars (the rate of decline in value terms, 
compared to the same period in 2020, respectively, amounted to 19.1%).

market management. An important role in this process is played by the 
development of foreign economic activity as the end result of the policy 
implemented in the country, which directly affects the standard of living of the 
population.

to the same period in 2020, decreased  
by 657.6 million US dollars (a decrease

 In the structure of imports of the republic, a significant share is noted in the 
city of Tashkent, which is 49.2%, or 791.5 million US dollars. 
The smallest share was recorded in Kashkadarya - 0.9%, or 14.3 million US 
dollars.  
The quarantine restrictions imposed during the 
pandemic have also impacted the service sector.  
In particular, as a result of restrictions on  
the transit of international traffic by the countries 
of the near and far abroad, the import  
of transport services decreased by 3.2 times and 
amounted to 8.4 million US dollars. 
At the same time, compared to 2020,  
the import of some services increased.  
In particular, imports of other business services 
reached 6.2 million US dollars (an increase  
of 28.9%), maintenance and repair services 
increased 2.1 times and amounted to 1.0 million 
US dollars.

in January 2021 amounted to 55.8 million US

transport services (15.0%), other business 
services (11.1%) and telecommunications, 
computer and information services (9.8%) 
account for the bulk of imports of services. In 
addition, other services accounted for 8.4% 
of total imports of services, including a high 
share of fees for the use of intellectual 
property (3.9%), maintenance and repair 
services (1.7%), services to individuals and 
services in the field of culture and recreation 
(1.3%), etc.

      It is important to note that the increasing volume of imports of machinery 
and equipment is a reflection of the industrialization policy, as well as active 
reform to support foreign direct investment in the creation, modernization and 
increase of production capacities. 
MAIN COUNTRIES - PARTNERS EXPORTING MACHINES  
AND TRANSPORTATION EQUIPMENT TO THE REPUBLIC  
OF UZBEKISTAN (for January 2021)  
IMPORT OF MACHINES  
AND TRANSPORTATION EQUIPMENT 
30 
At the end of January 2021, the volume of machinery and transport 
equipment in the structure of imports reached 538.4 million US dollars and 
decreased, compared to the same period in 2020, by 12.6%, in general,  
the share in the total volume of imports was 33.5 %. 
The decrease in the volume of imports of machinery and transport equipment 
was due to machinery specially designed for specific industries (by 27.7%),  
as well as non-specialized machinery and equipment for industry (by 17.9%). 
MAIN PARTNER COUNTRIES EXPORTING INDUSTRIAL 
PRODUCTS TO THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN 
(for January 2021) 
IMPORT OF INDUSTRIAL GOODS 
At the end of January 2021, the volume of industrial goods in the structure 
of imports reached 272.5 million US dollars and increased by 6.2% compared  
to the same period in 2020, in general, the share in the total volume of imports 
was 16.9%. 
31 
The main imports of industrial goods are in cast iron and non-alloy steel 
products (63.8 million US dollars), rubber tires and tubes for all types of wheels 
(8.3 million US dollars), aluminum (9.1 million US dollars), paper and cardboard 
(14.8 million US dollars), plywood, particle board, other processed wood  
(17.0 million US dollars), etc.

sectors of the country's economy. 
According to preliminary data, the volume of market services 
provided in January-November 2022 increased by 65 457.7 billion 
soums and reached 322 643.2 billion soums.  
In comparable terms, compared to January-November 2021 
(119.8%), the growth rate was 116.0%.

Today, the service sector plays a decisive role in the economy 
of developed countries. In Uzbekistan, the tertiary sector, as the 
service sector is sometimes called, is one of the fastest growing 
sectors of the country's economy.  
According to preliminary data, the volume of market services 
provided in January-October 2022 increased by 58 890.0 billion 
soums and reached 289 671.0 billion soums.  
In comparable terms, compared to January-October 2021 
(119.4%), the growth rate was 116.5%.

6 
Preliminary data 
for January-March 2022  
In the structure of market services provided by type of economic activity, 
trade services account for the largest share. In January-March 2022, their 
share was 25.2%. At the same time, high rates were noted in financial services 
(24.6%), transport (20.9%), communication and informatization services (6.4%), 
as well as in education (3.9%). 
A slight increase in volumes was noted in the provision of computer repair 
services, the share of which reached only 1.7%. 
For comparison: in January-March 2021, trade services in the total 
amounted to 25.7%. During this period, the share of computer repair services 
was also minimal - 1.7%. 
 
 
 
Growth in financial services by 37.6% (contribution to the growth of the total 
volume of services rendered 8.3 points), transport services by 11.6% 
(contribution to the growth of 2.6 points), trade services by 8.6% (contribution to 
the growth 2.2 points), as well as communication and informatization services 
by 27.8% (contribution to the growth of 1.7 points) had an impact on the growth 
of the total volume of services rendered.  
In January-March 2022, compared to the same period last year, the growth 
rate in comparable prices amounted to 115.9%. 
The main factor behind the slight increase in the total volume of services 
rendered is the reduction in services in the field of education by 5.0% (their 
negative impact was 0.2 points) and services related to rent and rental by 4.3% 
(-0.1 points).

1 395.7 million US dollars, or 8.3% of its total volume, and increased by 
65.5% compared to the same period in 2021. As part of the import                      
of services, the main share is occupied by travel (tourism - 55.1%), 
transport services (14.7%), telecommunications, computer and information 
services (10.1%), other business services (6.8%).

of services, including a high share of fees for the use of intellectual property 
(4.7%), construction services (3.1%), maintenance and repair services (2.7%), 
etc.

dollars and increased by 23.6% compared to the same period in 2021, in 
general, the share in total imports amounted to 33.2%.

of services, the main share is occupied by travel (tourism - 59.0%), 
transport services (14.2%), other business services (9.0%), 
telecommunications, computer and information services (5.9%).

including a high share of fees for the use of intellectual property (4.1%), 
construction services (3.6%), maintenance and repair services (2.1%), etc.

dollars and increased by 51.9% compared to the same period in 2021;  
in general, the share in the total volume of imports amounted to 35.2%.

computer and information services (5.7%).

dollars and increased by 63.6% compared to the same period in 2021;  
in general, the share in the total import volume amounted to 34.6%.

The volume of financial services is taken into account by the volume
of interest income received from financial intermediation (in the amount
of payment for them), as well as in the form of fees for the services of a financial
institution in providing a loan or maintaining a deposit.
The volume of transport services is the amount of income from
transportation and other activities directly related to the implementation of the
transport process (loading and unloading, freight forwarding services, transport
maintenance, etc.) by type of transport.
Road transport services include all land passenger transport, excluding
rail transport, other land passenger transport services and road transport
services for freight transport, as well as relocation services.
The volume of trade services, including electronic ones, is gross
income, which is the difference between the sales and purchase prices of goods
sold. If a transaction for the purchase and sale of goods is carried out in the
interests of another person on the basis of contracts, orders, commissions or
agency agreements, the cost of services is reflected in the amount
of remuneration.
The volume of communication and information services at current
prices is determined as the sum of the income of enterprises and organizations
(in the amount of revenue from their sales) providing services in this area.
Telecommunications services are the provision of telecommunications
and other related services, in particular such as the transmission of voice, text,
audio or video data.
The “Education” section includes public and private education at any
level and training in any profession, full-time or part-time, as well as via Internet
channels and through postal correspondence. This includes education provided
by institutions within the regular school system at various levels, as well as adult
education (training and retraining courses), auxiliary activities in the field
of education, etc. When carrying out activities in the field of education, the cost
of market services provided, including distance learning (contractual), is
reflected.
Explanations for statistical indicators 
of the service sector
The volume of healthcare services is the cost of market services
provided for various types of medical care and sanitary services by healthcare
institutions.
The volume of services for the provision of food and beverages is the
cost of turnover, which includes, in addition to the realized overlay, the cost
of products used in food preparation and sold without processing.
The scope of accommodation services includes the cost of services
provided for the provision of places for short-term accommodation (hotels,
hotels, motels, etc.).
When providing services related to real estate, the cost of services
related to operations on real estate, from the leasing of own real estate that is
under economic management, operational management or leased, is indicated.
The output of rent and rental services is determined in the amount
of revenue from the rental of machinery and equipment without an operator,
rental of household products and personal items.
The volume of computer and household repair services is the amount
of revenue from market services provided for repair, maintenance of computers
and peripheral equipment, repair of communications equipment, consumer
electronics, home and garden equipment, footwear and leather goods, furniture
and household accessories, clothing and accessories, sporting goods, musical
instruments, hobby items and other personal and household items.
The volume of services in the field of architecture, engineering
surveys and the provision of technical advice includes the cost of design,
survey, design, technological works and services performed in accordance with
the requirements stipulated in the contract, as well as the cost of construction
supervision and other engineering services performed in-house.

consumer services.

The volume of financial services is taken into account by the volume
of interest income received from financial intermediation (in the amount
of payment for them), as well as in the form of fees for the services of a financial
institution in providing a loan or maintaining a deposit.
The volume of transport services is the amount of income from
transportation and other activities directly related to the implementation of the
transport process (loading and unloading, freight forwarding services, transport
maintenance, etc.) by type of transport.
Road transport services include all land passenger transport, excluding
rail transport, other land passenger transport services and road transport
services for freight transport, as well as relocation services.
The volume of trade services, including electronic ones, is gross
income, which is the difference between the sales and purchase prices of goods
sold. If a transaction for the purchase and sale of goods is carried out in the
interests of another person on the basis of contracts, orders, commissions or
agency agreements, the cost of services is reflected in the amount
of remuneration.
The volume of communication and information services at current
prices is determined as the sum of the income of enterprises and organizations
(in the amount of revenue from their sales) providing services in this area.
Telecommunications services are the provision of telecommunications
and other related services, in particular such as the transmission of voice, text,
audio or video data.
The “Education” section includes public and private education at any
level and training in any profession, full-time or part-time, as well as via Internet
channels and through postal correspondence. This includes education provided
by institutions within the regular school system at various levels, as well as adult
education (training and retraining courses), auxiliary activities in the field
of education, etc. When carrying out activities in the field of education, the cost
of market services provided, including distance learning (contractual), is
reflected.
Explanations for statistical indicators 
of the service sector
The volume of healthcare services is the cost of market services
provided for various types of medical care and sanitary services by healthcare
institutions.
The volume of services for the provision of food and beverages is the
cost of turnover, which includes, in addition to the realized overlay, the cost
of products used in food preparation and sold without processing.
The scope of accommodation services includes the cost of services
provided for the provision of places for short-term accommodation (hotels,
hotels, motels, etc.).
When providing services related to real estate, the cost of services
related to operations on real estate, from the leasing of own real estate that is
under economic management, operational management or leased, is indicated.
The output of rent and rental services is determined in the amount
of revenue from the rental of machinery and equipment without an operator,
rental of household products and personal items.
The volume of computer and household repair services is the amount
of revenue from market services provided for repair, maintenance of computers
and peripheral equipment, repair of communications equipment, consumer
electronics, home and garden equipment, footwear and leather goods, furniture
and household accessories, clothing and accessories, sporting goods, musical
instruments, hobby items and other personal and household items.
The volume of services in the field of architecture, engineering
surveys and the provision of technical advice includes the cost of design,
survey, design, technological works and services performed in accordance with
the requirements stipulated in the contract, as well as the cost of construction
supervision and other engineering services performed in-house.

The volume of financial services is taken into account by the volume of
interest income received from financial intermediation (in the amount of payment
for them), as well as in the form of fees for the services of a financial institution in
providing a loan or maintaining a deposit.
The volume of transport services is the amount of income from
transportation and other activities directly related to the implementation of the
transport process (loading and unloading, freight forwarding services, transport
maintenance, etc.) by type of transport.
Road transport services include all land passenger transport, excluding
rail transport, other land passenger transport services and road transport
services for freight transport, as well as relocation services.
The volume of trade services, including electronic ones, is gross
income, which is the difference between the sales and purchase prices of goods
sold. If a transaction for the purchase and sale of goods is carried out in the
interests of another person on the basis of contracts, orders, commissions or
agency agreements, the cost of services is reflected in the amount of
remuneration.
The volume of communication and information services at current
prices is determined as the sum of the income of enterprises and organizations
(in the amount of revenue from their sales) providing services in this area.
Telecommunications services are the provision of telecommunications
and other related services, in particular such as the transmission of voice, text,
audio or video data.
The “Education” section includes public and private education at any
level and training in any profession, full-time or part-time, as well as via Internet
channels and through postal correspondence. This includes education provided
by institutions within the regular school system at various levels, as well as adult
education (training and retraining courses), auxiliary activities in the field of
education, etc. When carrying out activities in the field of education, the cost of
market services provided, including distance learning (contractual), is reflected.
Glossary
The volume of healthcare services is the cost of market services
provided for various types of medical care and sanitary services by healthcare
institutions.
The volume of services for the provision of food and beverages is the
cost of turnover, which includes, in addition to the realized overlay, the cost of
products used in food preparation and sold without processing.
The scope of accommodation services includes the cost of services
provided for the provision of places for short-term accommodation (hotels,
hotels, motels, etc.).
When providing services related to real estate, the cost of services
related to operations on real estate, from the leasing of own real estate that is
under economic management, operational management or leased, is indicated.
The output of rent and rental services is determined in the amount of
revenue from the rental of machinery and equipment without an operator, rental
of household products and personal items.
The volume of computer and household repair services is the amount
of revenue from market services provided for repair, maintenance of computers
and peripheral equipment, repair of communications equipment, consumer
electronics, home and garden equipment, footwear and leather goods, furniture
and household accessories, clothing and accessories, sporting goods, musical
instruments, hobby items and other personal and household items.
The volume of services in the field of architecture, engineering
surveys and the provision of technical advice includes the cost of design,
survey, design, technological works and services performed in accordance with
the requirements stipulated in the contract, as well as the cost of construction
supervision and other engineering services performed in-house.

The volume of financial services is taken into account by the volume of
interest income received from financial intermediation (in the amount of payment
for them), as well as in the form of fees for the services of a financial institution in
providing a loan or maintaining a deposit.
The volume of transport services is the amount of income from
transportation and other activities directly related to the implementation of the
transport process (loading and unloading, freight forwarding services, transport
maintenance, etc.) by type of transport.
Road transport services include all land passenger transport, excluding
rail transport, other land passenger transport services and road transport
services for freight transport, as well as relocation services.
The volume of trade services, including electronic ones, is gross
income, which is the difference between the sales and purchase costs of goods
sold. If a transaction for the purchase and sale of goods is carried out in the
interests of another person on the basis of contracts, orders, commissions or
agency agreements, the cost of services is reflected in the amount of
remuneration.
The volume of communication and information services at current
prices is determined as the sum of the income of enterprises and organizations
(in the amount of revenue from their sales) providing services in this area.
Telecommunications services are the provision of telecommunications
and other related services, in particular such as the transmission of voice, text,
audio or video data.
The “Education” section includes public and private education at any
level and training in any profession, full-time or part-time, as well as via Internet
channels and through postal correspondence. This includes education provided
by institutions within the regular school system at various levels, as well as adult
education (training and retraining courses), auxiliary activities in the field of
education, etc. When carrying out activities in the field of education, the cost
of market services provided, including distance learning (contractual), is
reflected.
Glossary

The volume of healthcare services is the cost of market services
provided for various types of medical care and sanitary services by healthcare
institutions.
The volume of services for the provision of food and beverages is the
cost of turnover, which includes, in addition to the realized overlay, the cost of
products used in food preparation and sold without processing.
The scope of accommodation services includes the cost of services
provided for the provision of places for short-term accommodation (hotels,
hotels, motels, etc.).
When providing services related to real estate, the cost of services
related to operations on real estate, from the leasing of own real estate that is
under economic management, operational management or leased, is indicated.
The output of rent and rental services is determined in the amount of
revenue from the rental of machinery and equipment without an operator, rental
of household products and personal items.
The volume of computer and household repair services is the amount
of revenue from market services provided for repair, maintenance of computers
and peripheral equipment, repair of communications equipment, consumer
electronics, home and garden equipment, footwear and leather goods, furniture
and household accessories, clothing and accessories, sporting goods, musical
instruments, hobby items and other personal and household items.
The scope of services in the field of architecture, engineering surveys
and technical consultations includes the cost of design, survey, engineering,
technological work and services performed in accordance with the requirements
stipulated in the contract, as well as the cost of construction supervision and
other engineering services carried out in-house.

Key indicators of the service sector in the Republic of Uzbekistan
The volume of financial services is taken into account by the volume of
interest income received from financial intermediation (in the amount of payment
for them), as well as in the form of fees for the services of a financial institution in
providing a loan or maintaining a deposit.
The volume of transport services is the amount of income from
transportation and other activities directly related to the implementation of the
transport process (loading and unloading, freight forwarding services, transport
maintenance, etc.) by type of transport.
Road transport services include all land passenger transport, excluding
rail transport, other land passenger transport services and road transport
services for freight transport, as well as relocation services.
The volume of trade services, including electronic ones, is gross income,
which is the difference between the sales and purchase costs of goods sold. If
a transaction for the purchase and sale of goods is carried out in the interests of
another person on the basis of contracts, orders, commissions or agency
agreements, the cost of services is reflected in the amount of remuneration.
The volume of communication and information services at current
prices is determined as the sum of the income of enterprises and organizations
(in the amount of revenue from their sales) providing services in this area.
Telecommunications services are the provision of telecommunications
and other related services, in particular such as the transmission of voice, text,
audio or video data.
The “Education” section includes public and private education at any
level and training in any profession, full-time or part-time, as well as via Internet
channels and through postal correspondence. This includes education provided
by institutions within the regular school system at various levels, as well as adult
education (training and retraining courses), auxiliary activities in the field of
education, etc. When carrying out activities in the field of education, the cost
of market services provided, including distance learning (contractual),
is reflected.
Glossary
The volume of healthcare services is the cost of market services
provided for various types of medical care and sanitary services by healthcare
institutions.
The volume of services for the provision of food and beverages is the
cost of turnover, which includes, in addition to the realized overlay, the cost of
products used in food preparation and sold without processing.
The scope of accommodation services includes the cost of services
provided for the provision of places for short-term accommodation (hotels,
motels, etc.).
When providing services related to real estate, the cost of services
related to operations on real estate, from the leasing of own real estate that is
under economic management, operational management or leased, is indicated.
The output of rent and rental services is determined in the amount of
revenue from the rental of machinery and equipment without an operator, rental
of household products and personal items.
The volume of computer and household repair services is the amount
of revenue from market services provided for repair, maintenance of computers
and peripheral equipment, repair of communications equipment, consumer
electronics, home and garden equipment, footwear and leather goods, furniture
and household accessories, clothing and accessories, sporting goods, musical
instruments, hobby items and other personal and household items.
The scope of services in the field of architecture, engineering surveys
and technical consultations includes the cost of design, survey, engineering,
technological work and services performed in accordance with the requirements
stipulated in the contract, as well as the cost of construction supervision and
other engineering services carried out in-house.

Glossary
The volume of financial services is recorded in terms of the volume of
interest income received from financial intermediation (in the amount of payment
for them), as well as in the form of a fee for the services of a financial institution
in providing a loan or maintaining a deposit.
The volume of transport services is the amount of income from
transportation and other activities directly related to the implementation of the
transport process (loading and unloading, forwarding services, transport
services, etc.) by type of transport.
Road transport services include all land passenger transport services,
excluding rail transport, other land passenger transport services and road
transport services for freight transport, as well as moving services.
The volume of trade services, including electronic ones, is the gross
income, which is the difference between the sale and purchase value of goods
sold. In the case of a transaction for the sale of goods in the interests of another
person on the basis of agreements, commissions or agency agreements, the
cost of services is reflected in the amount of remuneration.
The volume of communication and informatization services at current
prices is defined as the sum of incomes of enterprises and organizations (in the
amount of proceeds from their sale) that provide services in this area.
Telecommunication services are the provision of telecommunications
and other related services, in particular such as the transmission of voice, text,
sound or video data.
The section "Education" includes public, private education of any level
and training of any profession, full-time or part-time, as well as through Internet
channels and through mail.
This includes education provided by institutions within the regular school
system at various levels, as well as adult education (training and retraining
courses), educational support activities, etc.
When carrying out activities in the field of education, the cost of the
rendered market services, including distance learning (contract) is reflected.

Glossary
The volume of health care services is the value of the market services
provided for various types of medical care and sanitation by health care facilities.
The volume of food and beverage services is the value of turnover,
which includes, in addition to the realized overlay, the value of the products used
in the preparation of food and sold without processing.
The scope of accommodation services includes the cost of services
rendered for the provision of places for short-term accommodation (hotels,
hotels, motels, etc.).
The output of rent and rental services is determined in the amount of
proceeds from the rental of machinery and equipment without an operator, the
rental of household goods and personal items.
The volume of computer and household goods repair services is the
amount of revenue from the rendered market services for the repair,
maintenance of computers and peripheral equipment, repair of communication
equipment, consumer electronics, home and garden equipment, shoes and
leather goods, furniture and household items, clothing and accessories, sporting
goods, musical instruments, hobbies and other personal and household items.
The volume of services in the field of architecture, engineering surveys
and the provision of technical advice includes the cost of design, survey,
design, technological works and services performed in accordance with the
requirements stipulated in the contract, as well as the cost of construction
supervision and other engineering services performed in-house.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more experience 
in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a competitive 
advantage in global trade. 
 As a result of the measures taken in the republic in recent years to 
stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balanced 
foreign trade, in January-December 2023 the foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 62.6 billion US dollars and increased compared to the 
same period in 2022, by 12.1 billion US dollars, or by 23.9%. 
1 
FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January-December 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their exportation (export) outside 
the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system  
of accounting for foreign trade.  
 
 
Of the total FTT volume, exports amounted to 24 426.2 million US dollars 
(an increase of 23.8% was noted by January-December 2023), and imports 
amounted to 38 141.2 million US dollars (an increase of 24.0%). As a result, 
the balance of foreign trade turnover amounted to a negative balance in the 
amount of -13 715.0 million US dollars.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more experience 
in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a competitive 
advantage in global trade. 
 As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balanced 
foreign trade, in January-November 2023 the foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 57.3 billion US dollars and increased compared to the 
same period of last year, by 11.9 billion US dollars, or by 26.2%.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January-November 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their exportation (export) outside 
the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system  
of accounting for foreign trade.  
 
Of the total FTT volume, exports amounted to 23 204.3 million US dollars 
(an increase of 30.6% was noted by January-November 2023), and imports 
amounted to 34 105.8 million US dollars (an increase of 23.3%). As a result, 
the balance of foreign trade turnover amounted to a negative balance  
of -10 901.5 million US dollars.

industry for Uzbekistan, light industry provides a high level of employment, and 
also contributes to the industrial potential and international reputation of our 
country.

undertaken to produce finished goods instead of raw cotton and create added 
value.

finished products to find their place in world markets.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more experience 
in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a competitive 
advantage in global trade. 
 As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the balance 
of foreign trade, in January-October 2023, foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 51.0 billion US dollars and increased, compared to the 
same period last year, by 10.3 billion US dollars, or by 25.2%. 
1 
FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January-October 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) outside the 
customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system  
of accounting for foreign trade. 
  
 
Of the total FTT volume, exports amounted to 20 470.2 million US dollars 
(by January-October 2023, an increase of 29.1% was noted), and imports –  
30 503.6 million US dollars (an increase of 22.7%). As a result, the balance  
of foreign trade turnover amounted to a negative balance in the amount  
of -10 033.3 million US dollars.

 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more experience 
in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a competitive 
advantage in global trade. 
 
 As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the balance 
of foreign trade, in January-September 2023, foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 44.8 billion US dollars and increased, compared to the 
same period last year, by 8.1 billion US dollars, or by 22.1%.

Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) outside the 
customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system  
of accounting for foreign trade.

management system, labor productivity increases, which, in turn, allows 
finished products to find their place in world markets.

to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the balance 
of foreign trade, in January-August 2023, foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 40.0 billion US dollars and increased, compared to the 
same period last year, by 7.5 billion US dollars, or by 23.2%.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January-August 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export outside the customs 
territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system of accounting for 
foreign trade. 
 
 
Of the total FTT volume, exports amounted to 16 434.6 million US dollars 
(an increase of 27.8% was noted by January-August 2023), and imports 
amounted to 23 611.0 million US dollars (an increase of 20.2%). As a result, 
the balance of foreign trade turnover amounted to a negative balance of  
-7 176.4 million US dollars.
