FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase the export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in foreign markets. Ultimately, they will have a competitive 
advantage in world trade. 
 As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balance of 
foreign trade, in January-July 2023, the foreign trade turnover in the country 
amounted to 35.0 billion US dollars and increased compared to with the 
same period last year, by 6.6 billion US dollars, or 23.3%. 
1 
FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(January-July 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover– is the sum of the value of a country's exports and imports 
over a given period. The statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from the stocks of material resources as a result of their import 
(import) into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) 
outside the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of the general 
foreign trade accounting system.  
 
Of the total volume of the FTT, exports amounted to 14 954.4 million US    
        dollars (by January-July 2023, an increase of 31.0% was noted), and 
imports – 20 021.4 million US dollars (an increase of 18.1% ). As a result, the 
balance of foreign trade turnover was negative in the amount of -5 067.0 
million US dollars.

dollars, or by 19.4%.

EXPORT OF TEXTILE PRODUCTS  
In recent years, the light industry has seen the development of high 
value-added products. Being an economically important industry for 
Uzbekistan, the light industry provides a high level of employment, and also 
contributes to the industrial potential and international prestige of our country. 
 
The increase in textile exports can be seen as a result of reforms aimed 
at producing finished goods instead of raw cotton and creating added value.

The volume of exports of services in January-June 2023 amounted to  
2 285.1 million US dollars, or 18.8% of the total volume of trade exports and 
increased by 41.4% compared to the same period in 2022. As part of the export 
of services, the lion's share is occupied by travel (tourism) (45.7%), transport 
services (37.8%), telecommunications, computer and information services 
(7.0%), other business services (4.4%). At the same time, for other services 
(5.1%), the largest share, respectively, falls on insurance and pension services 
(1.9%), financial services (1.3%), fees for the use of intellectual property (0.8%) 
and etc. 
As a result of the widespread use of new production technologies and 
modern equipment in the country, as well as the introduction of a quality 
management system, labor productivity is increasing, which, in turn, allows 
finished products to find their place in world markets.

 During the reporting period, imports amounted to 17 030.5 million US 
dollars (an increase in growth rates, compared to January-June 2022, 
amounted to 17.0%). The main share in its structure is occupied by machinery 
and transport equipment (37.8%), industrial goods (16.3%), as well as 
chemicals and similar products (13.3%). 
IMPORT OF THE REPUBLIC OF UZBEKISTAN 
The analysis of the dynamics of imports of goods also showed that  
in January-June 2023, compared with the same period in 2022, the volume  
of imports of goods increased by 2 474.6 million US dollars and amounted  
to 17 030.5 million US dollars, and imports of services reached 1 015.6 million 
US dollars.

Foreign trade turnover – is the sum of the value of exports and 
imports of the country for a certain period. The statistics of foreign trade in

stocks of material resources as a result of their import (import) into the 
customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) 
outside the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis

 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase the export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in foreign markets. Ultimately, they will have a competitive 
advantage in world trade. 
 As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the balance 
of foreign trade, in January-April 2023, foreign trade turnover in the country 
amounted to 19.6 billion US dollars and increased by 2.3 billion US 
dollars, or by 13.4%. 
1 
FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January-April 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the value of exports and imports 
of the country for a certain period. The statistics of foreign trade in goods 
keeps records of goods that are added to or subtracted from the stocks of 
material resources as a result of their import (import) into the customs 
territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) outside the 
customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of the general 
foreign trade accounting system.  
 
 
Of the total volume of the FTT, exports amounted to 7 660.8 million US 
dollars (by January-April 2023, an increase of 6.2% was noted), and imports 
– 11 916.2 million US dollars (an increase of 18.6%). As a result, the balance 
of foreign trade turnover was negative in the amount of -4 255.4 million US 
dollars.

 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase the export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in foreign markets. Ultimately, they will have a competitive 
advantage in world trade.  
As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the balance

amounted to 14.8 billion US dollars and increased by 1.6 billion US 
dollars, or by 11.9%.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER  
(for January-March 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the value of exports and imports 
of the country for a certain period. The statistics of foreign trade in goods 
keeps records of goods that are added to or subtracted from the stocks of 
material resources as a result of their import (import) into the customs 
territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) outside the 
customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of the general 
foreign trade accounting system. 
 
Of the total volume of the FTT, exports amounted to 5 688.9 million US 
dollars (against January-March 2023, there was a decrease of 2.6%), and 
imports – 9 090.8 million US dollars (an increase of 23.4%). As a result, the 
balance of foreign trade turnover was negative in the amount of -3 401.9 
million US dollars.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase the export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in foreign markets. Ultimately, they will have a competitive 
advantage in world trade. 
As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent years 
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the balance 
of foreign trade, in January-February 2023, foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 8.9 billion US dollars and increased by 176.4 million 
US dollars, or by 2.0%. 
1 
FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January-February 2023, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the value of exports and imports 
of the country for a certain period. The statistics of foreign trade in goods 
keeps records of goods that are added to or subtracted from the stocks of 
material resources as a result of their import into the customs territory of the 
Republic of Uzbekistan or their export outside the customs territory of the 
Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of the general foreign trade 
accounting system. 
 
Of the total FTT volume, exports amounted to 3 164.6 million US 
dollars (against January-February 2023, there was a decrease of 23.7%), 
and imports – 5 783.3 million US dollars (an increase of 25.1%). As a 
result, the balance of foreign trade turnover was negative in the amount  
of -2 618.6 million US dollars.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER
The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid
growth of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions
taken to increase the export potential will allow local companies to gain
more experience in foreign markets. Ultimately, they will have a competitive
advantage in world trade.
As a result of the measures implemented in the republic in recent
years to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure the
balance of foreign trade, in January 2023, foreign trade turnover in the
country amounted to 5.0 billion US dollars and increased by 1.5 billion US
dollars, or 42.0%, compared to the same period last year.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER
(for January 2023, million US dollars)
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the value of exports and imports
of the country for a certain period. The statistics of foreign trade in goods
keeps records of goods that are added to or subtracted from the stocks of
material resources as a result of their import (import) into the customs
territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their export (export) outside the
customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of the general
foreign trade accounting system.

dollars (an increase of 45.1% compared to January 2023), and imports
amounted to 2 959.7 million US dollars (an increase of 39.8%). As a result,
the balance of foreign trade turnover was negative in the amount of -876.9
million US dollars.

The most important factor in the attractive geostrategic position of 
Uzbekistan is the presence of a developed system of transport 
communications. At present, the country's transport system fully meets 
domestic transportation needs. 
The existing networ k of rail and road transport communications not 
only reliably connects the most remote areas and settlements of the 
republic, provides access to international transport systems, but also 
provides wide access to the main sources of natural and mineral 
resources of the country.  
Uzbekistan is favorably located in terms of the development of 
international aviation communications. Being located between Europe and 
East Asia, the republic can serve as a very promising international 
transport hub providing transit air transportation of goods and passengers.

by road transport (49.2  %).  The share of transportation services through 
pipelines in January -November 2018 amounted to 17.6%. Services  
rendered by rail transport in the total volume of transport services account 
for 13.7 %.

The largest share in the total volume of transport services is provided by services 
rendered by motor transport (48.0%). This is due to maneuverability, mobility, the delivery 
of goods (passengers) "from door to door" without additional overloads or transplants 
along the way, as well as the autonomy of the vehicle's movement.  
Transportation services by pipeline account for 18.6% of the total transport services. 
Services rendered by railway transport in the total volume of transport services are 
16.5%. The share of services in the transportation of cargo and passengers by air has 
reached 10.0% of the total volume of transport services. Subsidiary transport activity 
occupies 6.9% of the total volume of transport services.  
 
Today, Uzbekistan possesses a huge transport potential and unique opportunities to 
meet the country's needs for the movement of both cargoes and passengers in all 
directions and all possible modes of transport.

The structure of transport services by mode of transport  
for January-February 2018, in %  
 Today, Uzbekistan has a huge transport potential and unique opportunities 
to meet the country's needs for transportation, both cargo and passengers in all 
directions and all possible modes of transport.  
The largest share in the total volume of transport services is provided by 
services provided by road transport (48.7%). This is due to maneuverability, 
mobility, mobility, delivery of goods (passengers) "from door to door" without 
additional overloads or transplantations along the way, autonomy of the 
vehicle's movement.  
Transportation services by pipelines occupy 17.5% in the total volume of 
transport services. Services rendered by rail make up 16.4% of the total volume 
of transport services. The share of services for transportation of cargo and 
passengers by air is 9.9% of the total volume of transport services. Subsidiary 
transport activity occupies 7.5% of the total volume of transport services.

reliable, and are also linked with a lower risk of loss or damage to goods. Along 
with this, for a number of perishable products and urgent goods, road transport is 
the only real mode of transportation. Because of this, road transport is the preferred 
means of transportation of agricultural products, textiles and other non -primary 
commodities exported from Uzbekistan.

According to the results of January-October 2024, textile exports 
amounted to 2 433.4 million US dollars, which amounted to 10.8 % of its total 
volume and, compared to the same period in 2023, it decreased by 5.7 %. 
In the structure of textile exports, the main share is also occupied by 
yarn (43.5 %) and finished textile products (39.1 %). Thus, in January-
October 2024, textile products were exported to 56 countries of the world. 
EXPORT OF TEXTILE PRODUCTS  
In recent years, the light industry has seen the development  
of high value-added production. Being an economically important sector  
for Uzbekistan, the light industry provides a high level of employment and also 
contributes to the industrial potential and international authority of our country. 
The increase in textile exports can be seen as a result of reforms carried 
out with the aim of producing finished goods instead of raw cotton and 
creating added value.

Due to the fact that the state pays great attention to the development
of agriculture and horticulture, the quality and volume of exported products are
increasing from year to year. In particular, in January-August 2024, 1 358.8
thousand tons of fruit and vegetable products were exported, and, compared to
the same period in 2023, this figure increased by 9.0 %, or 111.9 thousand
tons.
EXPORT OF FRUIT AND VEGETABLE PRODUCTS
The volume of exports of fruit and vegetable products in the period under
review amounted to 922.8 million US dollars (the growth rate, compared to the
same period in 2023, amounted to 20.8 %, respectively). In the total volume,
exports amounted to 5.3 %.
The main export markets for fruit and vegetable products were Russia
(44.1 %), Pakistan (15.2 %), Kazakhstan (14.6 %), and Afghanistan (6.6 %).

According to the results of January-August 2024, textile exports
amounted to 2 000.4 million US dollars, which amounted to 11.5 % of its total
volume and, compared to the same period in 2023, it decreased by -5.3 %.
In the structure of textile exports, the main share is also occupied by yarn
(44.8 %) and finished textile products (38.5 %). Thus, in January-August 2024,
textile products were exported to 56 countries of the world.
EXPORT OF TEXTILE PRODUCTS
In recent years, the light industry has seen the development of high
value-added production. Being an economically important sector for
Uzbekistan, the light industry provides a high level of employment and also
contributes to the industrial potential and international authority of our country.
The increase of volume of exports in textile can be seen as a result of
reforms carried out with the aim of producing finished goods instead of raw
cotton and creating added value.

growth of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions 
taken to increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a 
competitive advantage in global trade. 
 As a result of the measures taken in the republic in recent years to 
stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balanced

amounted to 31.8 billion US dollars and increased compared to the same 
period in 2023, by 2.5 billion US dollars, or 8.5%.

Based on the results of January-June 2024, textile products were 
exported in the amount of 1 532.2 million US dollars, which amounted to 11.8% 
of its total volume and, compared to the same period in 2023, it decreased  
by - 5.3%. 
In the structure of exports of textile products, the main share is also 
occupied by yarn (46.2%) and finished textile products (38.1%). Thus,  
in January-June 2024, 496 types of textile products were exported  
to 55 countries.. 
EXPORT OF TEXTILE PRODUCTS 
In recent years, the light industry has seen the development  
of production of products with high added value. As an economically important 
industry for Uzbekistan, light industry provides a high level of employment, and 
also contributes to the industrial potential and international reputation of our 
country. 
The increase in textile exports can be seen as a result of reforms 
undertaken to produce finished goods instead of raw cotton and create added 
value.

The volume of services exports for January-June 2024 amounted to  
3 124.3 million US dollars, or 24.0% of the total volume of trade exports and 
increased by 26.4% compared to the same period in 2023. The lion's share  
of services exports is made up of travel (tourism) (46.6%), transport services 
(38.0%), telecommunications, computer and information services (8.3%), and 
other business services (2.9%). At the same time, the largest share of other 
services (4.2%) is accounted for by financial services (1.1%), insurance and 
pension services (1.0%), construction services (0.7%), etc.  
As a result of the widespread use of new production technologies and 
modern equipment in the country, as well as the introduction of a quality 
management system, labor productivity is increasing, which, in turn, allows 
finished products to find their place in world markets.

of production of products with high added value. Being an economically 
important industry for Uzbekistan, light industry provides a high level  
of employment, and also contributes to the industrial potential and international 
reputation of our country.

out to produce finished goods instead of raw cotton and create added value.

The volume of exports of services in January-April 2024 amounted

export of services, the lion's share is occupied by transport services (44.0 %), 
travel (tourism) (41.2 %), telecommunications, computer and information 
services (9.1 %), and other business services (2.7 %). At the same time, for 
other services (3.1 %), the largest share respectively falls on insurance and 
pension services (1.3 %), financial services (0.9 %), government goods and 
services not classified as other categories ( 0.6 %) and etc. 
As a result of the widespread use of new production technologies and 
modern equipment in the country, as well as the introduction of a quality 
management system, labor productivity increases, which, in turn, allows 
finished products to find their place in world markets.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER  
 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken  
to increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have  
a competitive advantage in global trade. 
 As a result of the measures taken in the republic in recent years  
to stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balanced 
foreign trade, in January-March 2024 the foreign trade turnover  
in the country amounted to 15.8 billion US dollars and increased compared 
to the same period in 2023, by 927.9 million US dollars, or by 6.2%. 
1 
FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January - March 2024, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their exportation (export) outside 
the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system  
of accounting for foreign trade.  
 
 
Of the total FTT volume, exports amounted to 6 384.4 million US dollars 
(an increase of 10.0% was noted by January-March 2023), and imports 
amounted to 9 438.6 million (an increase of 3.8%). As a result, the balance  
of foreign trade turnover amounted to a negative balance in the amount  
of -3 054.2 million US dollars.

 The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid growth 
of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions taken to 
increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more experience 
in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a competitive 
advantage in global trade. 
As a result of the measures taken in the republic in recent years to 
stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balanced 
foreign trade, in January-February 2024 the foreign trade turnover in the 
country amounted to 9.9 billion US dollars and increased compared to the 
same period. period 2023, by 940.3 million US dollars, or by 10.5%.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
(for January - February 2024, million US dollars) 
Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports 
for a certain period. Statistics of foreign trade in goods keeps records of goods that are 
added to or subtracted from stocks of material resources as a result of their entry (import) 
into the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan or their exportation (export) outside 
the customs territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the basis of a general system  
of accounting for foreign trade.

amounted to 6 287.5 million US dollars (an increase of 8.7%). As a result, the 
balance of foreign trade turnover amounted to a negative balance of - 2 656.0 
million US dollars.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER  
  The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid 
growth of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions 
taken to increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in working in foreign markets. Ultimately they will have a 
competitive advantage in global trade. 
  As a result of the measures taken in the republic in recent years to 
stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, to ensure a balanced 
foreign trade, in January 2024 the foreign trade turnover in the country 
amounted to 4.2 billion US dollars and decreased compared to the same 
period 2023, by 870.1 million US dollars, or by 17.2%.

Foreign trade turnover is the sum of the values of a country's exports and imports

IV. Metadata 
When compiling statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic  
of Uzbekistan, along with the HS of FEA, the United Nations Standard International Trade 
Classification (SITC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes to group exported and 
imported goods into  10 major sections. The assignment of SITC codes to goods is carried out 
using conversion keys between the HS and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on foreign trade in goods and 
services: the initial data for foreign trade statistics are derived from customs cargo declarations 
of the Customs Committee and statistical observations of the National Statistics Committee on 
goods transferred from residents to non -residents that do not cross the state border and are not 
included in customs declarations; the compilation of foreign trade services statistics is carried 
out based on statistical observations. 
In some cases, minor discrepancies between the total and the sum of components are 
explained by data rounding.

IV. Metadata 
When compiling statistical indicator s on the Republic of Uzbekistan’ s foreign trade in 
goods, the United Nations Standard International Trade Classific ation (SITC) is used alongside 
the CN FEA. It allows for analytical grouping of exported and imported goods into 10 major 
sections. SITC codes are assigned to goods using transition keys between the CN FEA and 
SITC.   
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on foreig n trade in goods and 
services: the initial data for compiling foreign trade statistics are data from cargo customs 
declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations of the  National Statistics 
Committee on goods transferred from residents to non -residents that do not cross the state 
border and are not included in the customs declaration; statistics on foreign trade services are 
compiled based on statistical observations.

IV. METADATA 
When compiling statistical indicators on the Republic of Uzbekistan's foreign trade in goods, 
the United Nations Standard International Trade Classification (SITC) is used alongside  
the CN FEA. It allows for analytical grouping of exported and imported goods into 10 major 
sections. SITC codes are assigned to goods using transition keys between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on foreign trade in goods and  services: 
the initial data for compiling foreign trade statistics are data from cargo customs declarations of the 
Customs Committee and statistical observations of the National Statistics Committee on goods 
transferred from residents to non-residents that do not cross the state border and are not included in 
the customs declaration; statistics on foreign trade services are compiled based on statistical 
observations.

IV. METADATA 
In forming statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic of Uzbekistan, along with 
the CN FEA, the International Standard Trade Classification of the United Nations (ISTC) is used, which 
allows for analytical purposes to group exported and imported goods into 10 large sections. Assignment 
of SITC codes to goods is carried out using transition keys between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are formed on the basis of data on foreign trade in goods  
and services: the initial data for the formation of statistics on foreign trade in goods are data from cargo 
customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations  
of the National Statistics Committee on goods moved from residents to non -residents that do not cross 
the state border and are not included in the customs declaration; the formatio n  
of statistics on foreign trade services is carried out on the basis of statistical observations.

IV. METADATA 
In forming statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic of Uzbekistan, along with 
the CC FT, the International Standard Trade Classification of the United Nations (ISTC) is used, which 
allows for analytical purposes to group exported and imported goods into 10 large sections. Assignment 
of ISTC codes to goods is carried out using transition keys between the CC FT and ISTC. 
Foreign trade statistics are formed on the basis of data on foreign trade in goods and services: the 
initial data for the formation of statistics on foreign trade in goods are data  
from cargo customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations  
of the National Statistics Committee on goods moved from residents to non -residents that do not cross 
the state border and are not included in the customs declaration; th e formation  
of statistics on foreign trade services is carried out on the basis of statistical observations.

IV. METADATA 
In the formation of statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic of 
Uzbekistan, along with the CN FEA , the Standard International Trade Classification of the 
United Nations ( SITC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes to group exported and 
imported goods into 10 large sections. Assignment of SITC codes to goods is carried out using 
transition keys between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are formed on the basi s of data on foreign trade in goods and 
services: the initial data for the formation of statistics on foreign trade in goods are data from 
cargo customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations of the 
National Statistics Committee  on goods moved from residents to non -residents that do not 
cross the state border and are not included in the customs declaration; the formation of 
statistics on foreign trade services is carried out on the basis of statistical observations.

IV. METADATA 
In forming statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic of Uzbekistan, 
along with the CN FEA, the International Standard Trade Classification of the United Nations 
(SITC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes to group exported and imported goods 
into 10 large sections. Assignment of SITC codes to goods is carried out using transition keys 
between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are formed on the basis of data on foreign trade in goods and 
services: the initial data for the formation of statistics on foreign trade in goods are data on 
cargo customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations of the 
National Statistics Committee on goods moved from residents to non -residents that do not 
cross the state border and are not included in the customs declaration; the formation of 
statistics on foreign trade services is carried out on the basis of statistical observations.

IV. METADATA 
 In forming statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic of Uzbekistan, 
along with the TN FEA, the International Standard Trade Classification of the United Nations 
(ISTC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes to group exported a nd imported goods 
into 10 large sections. Assignment of ISTC codes to goods is carried out using transition keys 
between the TN FEA and ISTC. 
Foreign trade statistics are formed on the basis of data on foreign trade in goods and 
services: the initial data for the formation of statistics on foreign trade in goods are data  
from cargo customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical o bservations  
of the National Statistics Committee on goods moved from residents to non -residents that do 
not cross the state border and are not included in the customs declaration; the formation  
of statistics on foreign trade services is carried out on the basis of statistical observations.

IV. Methodological explanations 
* When forming statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic  
of Uzbekistan, along with the Commodity nomenclature of foreign economic activity , the 
International Standard Trade Classification of the United Nations (hereinafter referred to as 
SITC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes to group exported and i mported goods into 
10 major sections. Assignment of SITC codes to goods is carried out using transition keys 
between the Commodity nomenclature of foreign economic activity and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are formed on the basis of data on foreign trade  in goods and 
services: the initial data for the formation of statistics on foreign trade in goods are data on 
cargo Customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations of the 
National Statistics Committee on goods moved from residen ts to non -residents that do not 
cross the state border and are not included in the customs declaration; the formation  
of statistics on foreign trade services is carried out on the basis of statistical observations.

FOREIGN TRADE TURNOVER 
The economic reforms carried out in our republic serve the rapid 
growth of trade relations with foreign countries. In particular, the decisions 
taken to increase export potential will allow local companies to gain more 
experience in foreign markets. Ultimately, they will have a competitive 
advantage in world trade. 
 As a result of measures taken in the republic in recent years to 
stimulate exports, optimize imports and, in general, ensure a balanced 
foreign trade, in January 2025, the country's foreign trade turnover amounted 
to 4.5 billion US dollars and increased, compared to the same period in 
2024, by 297.2 million US dollars, or 7.1 %.

foreign economic partners of Uzbekistan (after China and Russia). The 
reasons for this are: the presence of a common border, trade in the CIS free 
trade zone, and the liberalization of mutual economic relations. 
Today, the Republic of Uzbekistan carries out trade relations with 154 
countries of the world. The largest volume of foreign trade turnover is recorded 
with China (22.1 %), Russia (17.7 %), Kazakhstan (7.0 %), Türkiye (4.7 %) 
and Germany (3.8 %).

I. Foreign trade turnover 
In January-August 2026, Uzbekistan's foreign trade turnover (FTT) amounted to USD 57,4 
billion, increasing by USD 4,0 billion, or 7,6%, compared with the corresponding period of 2025.  
 
 
 
Foreign trade turnover*, January-August, USD million 
 
 
Within total FTT, exports amounted to USD 22,9 billion (down 3,4% from January -

IV. Methodological notes 
 
In compiling Uzbekistan's foreign trade statistics for goods, both the Commodity 
Nomenclature of Foreign Economic Activity (CN FEA) and the United Nations Standard 
International Trade Classification (SITC) are used. SITC codes are assigned to goods using 
conversion keys between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled from data on trade in goods and services. Cargo 
customs declarations of the Customs Committee, together with the National Statistics 
Committee's statistical surveys covering goods that do not cross the state border or are not 
included in customs declarations, as well as goods transferred by residents to non -residents, 
constitute the source data for foreign trade in goods statistics; foreign trade in services statistics 
are compiled from statistical surveys. 
In some cases, minor differences between totals and the sum of their components are 
due to rounding.

IV. Methodological notes 
 
In compiling Uzbekistan's foreign trade statistics for goods, both the Commodity 
Nomenclature of Foreign Economic Activity (CN FEA) and the United Nations Standard 
International Trade Classification (SITC) are used. SITC codes are assigned to goods using 
conversion keys between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled from data on trade in goods and services. Cargo 
customs declarations of the Customs Committee, together with the National Statistics 
Committee's statistical surveys covering goods that do not cross the state border or are not 
included in customs declarations, as well as goods transferred by residents to non -residents, 
constitute the source data for foreign trade in goods statistics; foreign trade in services statistics 
are compiled from statistical surveys. 
In some cases, minor differences between totals and the sum of their components are 
due to rounding.

IV. Methodological notes 
 
In compiling Uzbekistan's foreign trade statistics for goods, both the Commodity 
Nomenclature of Foreign Economic Activity (CN FEA) and the United Nations Standard 
International Trade Classification (SITC) are used. SITC codes are assigned to goods using 
conversion keys between the CN FEA and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled from data on trade in goods and services. Cargo 
customs declarations of the Customs Committee, together with statistical surveys of the 
National Statistics Committee covering goods that do not cross the state border, are not included 
in customs declarations, and are transferred by residents to non -residents, constitute the source 
data for foreign trade in goods statistics. Foreign trade in services statistics are compiled from 
statistical surveys. 
In some cases, minor differences between totals and the sum of their components are 
due to rounding.

IV. Metadata  
 
 
When compiling statistical indicators on the foreign trade of goods of the Republic  
of Uzbekistan, the United Nations Standard International Trade Classification (SITC) is used  
in addition to the Commodity Nomenclature of Foreign Economic Activity (TN VED).  
The SITC allows for exported and imported goods to be grouped  
into 10 major sections for analytical purposes. SITC codes are assigned to goods using conversion 
keys between the TN VED and the SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on the foreign trade of goods  
and services. The source data for compiling statistics on the foreign trade of goods are cargo 
customs declarations from the Customs Committee and statistical observations  
from the National Statistics Committee on goods transferred from residents to non-residents that 
do not cross the state border and are not included in a customs de claration. Statistics  
on foreign trade in services are compiled based on statistical observations. 
In some cases, minor discrepancies between the total and the sum of its components  
are due to data rounding.

IV. Metadata 
 
When compiling statistical indicators on the foreign trade of goods of the Republic  
of Uzbekistan, the UN's Standard International Trade Classification (SITC) is used alongside the 
HS (Harmonized System), which allows for exported and imported goods to be grouped into 10 
major sections for analytical purposes. Goods are assigned SITC codes using conversion keys 
between the HS and the SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on foreign trade in goods  
and services. The primary data for compiling statistics on foreign trade in goods are data  
from cargo customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical observations  
of the National Statistics Committee on goods transferred from residents to non -residents  
that do not cross the state border and are not included in a customs declaration. Statistics  
on foreign trade in services are compiled based on statistical observations. 
In some cases, minor discrepancies between the total and the sum of its components  
are due to data rounding.

IV. Metadata 
 
When compiling statistical indicators on the foreign trade of goods of the Republic  
of Uzbekistan, the United Nations Standard International Trade Classification (SITC) is used  
in addition to the Commodity Nomenclature of Foreign Economic Activity (TN VED).  
The SITC allows for exported and imported goods to be grouped  
into 10 major sections for analytical purposes. SITC codes are assigned to goods using 
conversion keys between the TN VED and the SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on the foreign trade of goods  
and services. The source data for compiling statistics on the foreign trade of goods are cargo 
customs declarations from the Customs Committee and statistical observations  
from the National Statistics Committee on goods transferred from residents to non-residents that 
do not cross the state border and are not included in a customs declaration. Statistics  
on foreign trade in services are compiled based on statistical observations. 
In some cases, minor discrepancies between the total and the sum of its components  
are due to data rounding.

IV. Metadata 
 
In compiling statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic  
of Uzbekistan, along with the HS (Harmonized System), the United Nations Standard 
International Trade Classification (SITC) is used, which allows for analytical purposes to group 
exported and imported goods into 10 major sections. SITC codes are assigned to goods using 
concordance keys between the HS and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics are compiled based on data on foreig n trade in goods and 
services: the source data for compiling foreign trade statistics on goods are data from cargo 
customs declarations of the Customs Committee and statistical surveys of the National 
Statistics Committee on goods transferred from resident s to non -residents that do not cross  
the state border and are not included in customs declarations; foreign trade services statistics 
are compiled based on statistical surveys. 
In certain cases, minor discrepancies between the total and the sum of components are 
due to rounding of data.

IV. Metadata 
In compiling statistical indicators on foreign trade in goods of the Republic of Uzbekistan, 
along with the HS (Harmonized System), the United Nations Standard In ternational Trade 
Classification (SITC) is used, which allows, for analytical purposes, to group exported and 
imported goods into 10 broad sections. SITC codes are assigned to goods using concordance 
keys between the HS and SITC. 
Foreign trade statistics a re compiled on the basis of data on foreign trade in goods and 
services: the source data for compiling foreign trade in goods statistics are customs cargo 
declarations from the Customs Committee and statistical surveys of the National Statistics 
Committee on goods transferred from residents to non-residents that do not cross the state border 
and are not included in customs declarations; foreign trade services statistics are compiled on the 
basis of statistical surveys. 
In certain cases, minor discrepancies between the total and the sum of the components 
are due to rounding of data.

XIII. FOREIGN ECONOMIC ACTIVITY 
 
Foreign trade turnover . The government's reforms in recent years aimed at 
stimulating exports, optimizing imports and,  in general, the policy implemented in the 
country in order to achieve a balanced foreign trade have increased the Republic's foreign 
trade turnover (hereinafter referred to as FTT) amounting to 42.2 billion US dollars by the 
end of 2019 and increased by 8 .7 billion US dollars, or 26.2% more than the figures in 
2018. This result is recorded as the highest indicator in the country's history. 
Out of the total volume of FTT, exports reached 17.9 billion US dollars (growth 
rate-128.0 %), and imports – 24.3 billion US dollars (growth rate -124.9 %). The passive 
balance of foreign trade turnover in the amount of 6.4 billion US dollars was noted.

increase in the volume of exports and imports in 2019 compared to last year. Compared to 
the 2017 year, FTT increased by 1 .6 times, and imports (1 .9 times) grew faster than 
exports (1.3 times).
